Status.note:
Status of the existing unit.

Status:
- Open the EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx and go to the Operating sheet. Plant 56480, generator M1, reads status '(OP) Operating', nameplate 60.4 MW, operating year 2011, operating month 6. No planned retirement year is listed.
- This matches the current value, so nothing changes. The unit is still operating. I found no retirement, mothballing or owner change.

Backup Power.note:
Backup Power is no.

Where to find it:
- Open the Department of Natural Resources air permit 77214005A-P10 from June 2022 at https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_DownloadObject.aspx?id=1095448 . The permit lists processes P01A and P01B as 'Simple Cycle Combustion Turbine [P&W Swiftpac 60 unit], 30.25 MWe' that serve the city's electric system. These turbines are the unit M1.
- The same permit lists a separate 1502 horsepower diesel engine as an emergency engine, process P10. That engine is not part of unit M1 and is not a unit in GEM.
- The EIA-860M table lists the sector as Electric Utility, so the turbines sell power to the grid and are not a backup fleet for a data center. The value no stands.

units.notes: The unit is still operating per the September 2026 EIA-860M table. No retirement, mothballing or owner change was found. Backup Power no is now backed by the 2022 air permit.

source_log.note: EIA-860M September 2026, Operating sheet, plant 56480 generator M1 status OP, 60.4 MW, 2011.
